free_tier.stated: No free tier and no free trial on the site read; blocks start at 500 GB for $25, with a 1 TB block at $45.

per_object_cap.stated: no per-object cap is published; the unit of retrieval is a Usenet article, ~750 KB by convention, so a 1 TiB month is roughly 1.4 million article fetches
per_object_cap.notes: an article size is a protocol convention, not a vendor number

retention.stated: Up to 5,912+ days retention, in the specials banner

egress.terms: Unlimited speed, SSL servers in US and EU, 100 connections

interface_detail: NNTP over TLS on port 563; no HTTP or object API exists for the download path, so a user drives it through SABnzbd, NZBGet or nzbdav
tooling: SABnzbd, NZBGet or nzbdav over NNTP/TLS; any newsreader works because the protocol is the same everywhere, and no provider SDK is needed
chaining: A cheap unlimited layer on the UsenetExpress spool that stacks under an Omicron primary when a client wants 100 connections at the lowest monthly rate.

limits.value: soft 10 TB/month on unlimited plans, reset on request via support - reported, not on the vendor page

limits_note: 2026 specials: unlimited $50/year (100 connections), monthly unlimited $7.99, 250 GB/month $10 per 6 months. Blocks: 500 GB $25, 1 TB $45, 2 TB $75, all one-time.
binding_note: The vendor publishes no volume cap. The r/usenet map records a soft 10 TB/month ceiling that support resets on request; at 1 TiB/month that does not bind.

identity_cost.detail: Email plus a paid order; the site is a WHMCS storefront whose cart requires payment. No trial.

reliability_note: UsenetExpress reseller (news.thecubenet.com and europe.thecubenet.com). The 2 TB block at $75 is $37.50/TB, the cheapest UsenetExpress block found on a vendor page.
confidence_note: Prices and limits from the vendor home page read today.

evidence.proved: 'Unlimited Usenet $50/year 100 Connections'; '$1TB Block $45/one-time'; '500GB Block $25'; '2TB Big Block $75'; 'Monthly Unlimited $7.99'; up to 5,912+ days
Thundernews/Thecubenet have soft limits (10TB per month) on their unlimited plans, reset on request by support

notes: The yearly unlimited at $50 is cheaper per month than UsenetExpress's own $90, which is the normal shape of reseller pricing on this backbone.
